unitTitle: Reported Speech - Reported Statements - Say/Tell - Reported Questions

pairsWith.noteUz: Bu nazariya beti Coursebook 14-unit (Live and Let Live) grammatikasini takrorlaydi: ko'chirma gap, darak gaplar, zamon va vaqt so'zlari o'zgarishi.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 14-UNIT NAZARIYA (66-bet, PDF 65). Yuqorida chapda ko'k '14', sarlavha: 'Reported Speech - Reported Statements - Say/Tell - Reported Questions'. Och pushti ramka.

'Reported Speech': Direct speech is the exact words someone said. We use quotation marks (" ") in direct speech. '"I want to help," Mary said.' Reported speech is the exact meaning of what someone said, but not the exact words. We do not use quotation marks in reported speech. We can either use the word that after the introductory verb or we can omit it. 'Mary said (that) she wanted to help.' • When the introductory verb is in the present tense or when the sentence expresses something which is always true (general truth), there are no changes in the verb tenses in reported speech. Direct speech: 'She says "I love animals."' Reported speech: 'She says (that) she loves animals.' Direct speech: '"Rhinos live in eastern and southern Africa," said the teacher.' Reported speech: 'The teacher said (that) rhinos live in eastern and southern Africa.'
'Reported Statements': When we report statements (i.e. a positive or negative sentence), we use the verbs "say" or "tell" to introduce the statement. Pronouns (I, you, he etc, me, you, him etc, mine, yours, etc) and possessive adjectives (my, your, his etc) change according to the meaning. Direct speech: 'Ed said, "I live in Belfast."' Reported speech: 'Ed said (that) he lived in Belfast.' • When the introductory verb is in the past tense, the verb tenses change as follows: JADVAL Direct speech → Reported speech: Present Simple '"I want to go out," he said.' → Past Simple 'He said (that) he wanted to go out.' Present Continuous '"She is playing in the garden," he said.' → Past Continuous 'He said (that) she was playing in the garden.' Present Perfect '"They have bought a new house," he said.' → Past Perfect 'He said (that) they had bought a new house.' Past Simple '"He sent me flowers," she said.' → Past Perfect 'She said (that) he had sent her flowers.' Future Simple '"I'll order a new fridge," he said.' → Conditional (would) 'He said (that) he would order a new fridge.'
Certain words and time expressions change as follows: JADVAL: tonight, today, this week/month etc → that night, that day, that week/month etc; now → then, at the time; yesterday, last night/week etc → the day before, the previous night/week etc; tomorrow, next week/month etc → the following/next day, the next/following week/month etc; two days/months etc ago → two days/months etc before; this, these → that, those.

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '66'.

exercises.instructionEn: Direct speech is the exact words someone said. We use quotation marks in direct speech: 'I want to help,' Mary said. Reported speech is the exact meaning of what someone said, but not the exact words. We do not use quotation marks. We can either use the word that after the introductory verb or omit it: Mary said (that) she wanted to help. When the introductory verb is in the present tense or when the sentence expresses something which is always true (general truth), there are no changes in the verb tenses: She says 'I love animals.' → She says (that) she loves animals. 'Rhinos live in eastern and southern Africa,' said the teacher. → The teacher said (that) rhinos live in eastern and southern Africa.
exercises.instructionUz: To'g'ridan-to'g'ri nutq - kimningdir AYNAN so'zlari. Qo'shtirnoq ishlatiladi: 'Yordam bermoqchiman,' dedi Meri. Ko'chirma gap - aytilganning MA'NOSI, aynan so'zlari emas. Qo'shtirnoq ishlatilmaydi. Kirish fe'lidan keyin 'that' ishlatish yoki tushirib qoldirish mumkin: Meri yordam bermoqchi ekanini aytdi. Kirish fe'li HOZIRGI zamonda bo'lsa yoki gap HAR DOIM TO'G'RI narsani (umumiy haqiqat) ifodalasa, zamon O'ZGARMAYDI: U 'Hayvonlarni yaxshi ko'raman' deydi. → U hayvonlarni yaxshi ko'rishini aytadi. 'Karkidonlar sharqiy va janubiy Afrikada yashaydi,' dedi o'qituvchi. → O'qituvchi karkidonlar sharqiy va janubiy Afrikada yashashini aytdi.
exercises.explanationUz:
TO'G'RIDAN-TO'G'RI NUTQ va
  KO'ChIRMA GAP.

  TO'G'RIDAN-TO'G'RI (aynan so'zlar,
  qo'shtirnoq):
    "I want to help," Mary said.

  KO'ChIRMA (ma'no, qo'shtirnoqsiz):
    Mary said (THAT) she wanted to
    help.

  'that' - ixtiyoriy (bo'lsa ham,
  bo'lmasa ham bo'ladi).


ZAMON O'ZGARMAYDI - 2 HOLAT:

  1) Kirish fe'li HOZIRGI zamonda
     (says):
     She SAYS 'I love animals.' →
     She SAYS (that) she LOVES
     animals.

  2) UMUMIY HAQIQAT:
     'Rhinos LIVE in Africa,' said
     the teacher. → The teacher
     said rhinos LIVE in Africa.
     (hozir ham yashaydi)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Ko'chirma gap = '-ini aytdi':
  'yordam bermoqchi ekanini aytdi'.


⚠ 'A RHINO':

  = karkidon (rhinoceros).

Mary said (that) she wanted to help. (reported speech - no quotation marks)

exercises.instructionEn: When we report statements (a positive or negative sentence), we use the verbs 'say' or 'tell' to introduce the statement. Pronouns (I, you, he, me, you, him, mine, yours) and possessive adjectives (my, your, his) change according to the meaning: Ed said, 'I live in Belfast.' → Ed said (that) he lived in Belfast. When the introductory verb is in the past tense, the verb tenses change: Present Simple → Past Simple ('I want to go out,' he said. → He said he wanted to go out.); Present Continuous → Past Continuous ('She is playing in the garden,' he said. → He said she was playing in the garden.); Present Perfect → Past Perfect ('They have bought a new house,' he said. → He said they had bought a new house.); Past Simple → Past Perfect ('He sent me flowers,' she said. → She said he had sent her flowers.); Future Simple → Conditional (would) ('I'll order a new fridge,' he said. → He said he would order a new fridge.). Certain words and time expressions change: tonight, today, this week → that night, that day, that week; now → then, at the time; yesterday, last night/week → the day before, the previous night/week; tomorrow, next week/month → the following/next day, the next/following week/month; two days ago → two days before; this, these → that, those.
exercises.instructionUz: Darak gaplarni (tasdiq yoki inkor) ko'chirganda 'say' yoki 'tell' fe'llari ishlatiladi. Olmoshlar (I, you, he, me, him, mine, yours) va egalik sifatlari (my, your, his) ma'noga qarab o'zgaradi: Ed 'Men Belfastda yashayman' dedi. → Ed Belfastda yashashini aytdi. Kirish fe'li O'TGAN zamonda bo'lsa, zamonlar o'zgaradi: Present Simple → Past Simple; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect; Past Simple → Past Perfect; Future Simple (will) → would. Ba'zi so'zlar va vaqt ifodalari ham o'zgaradi: tonight/today/this week → that night/that day/that week; now → then; yesterday/last night → the day before/the previous night; tomorrow/next week → the following day/the following week; two days ago → two days before; this/these → that/those.
exercises.explanationUz:
KO'ChIRMA DARAK GAP - 3 O'ZGARISh.

  1) OLMOShLAR (ma'noga qarab):
     Ed said, "I live in Belfast."
     → Ed said (that) HE lived in
       Belfast.
     I → he/she; my → his/her; me →
     him/her; you → I/me ...

  2) ZAMON - BIR QADAM ORQAGA
     (kirish fe'li o'tgan zamonda):
     Present Simple → Past Simple
       "I WANT" → he WANTED
     Present Continuous → Past
       Continuous
       "She IS PLAYING" → she WAS
       PLAYING
     Present Perfect → Past Perfect
       "They HAVE BOUGHT" → they
       HAD BOUGHT
     Past Simple → Past Perfect
       "He SENT" → he HAD SENT
     Future (will) → WOULD
       "I'LL ORDER" → he WOULD
       ORDER

  3) VAQT SO'ZLARI:
     today/tonight → that day/that
       night
     now → then
     yesterday → the day before
     last week → the previous week
     tomorrow → the following/next
       day
     next week → the following week
     two days ago → two days before
     this/these → that/those


⚠ 'BELFAST':

  = Shimoliy Irlandiya poytaxti.

points.uz: Ed 'Men Belfastda yashayman' dedi. → Ed Belfastda yashashini aytdi. (I → he)

points.en: 'I want to go out,' he said. → He said (that) he wanted to go out. (Present Simple → Past Simple)
'She is playing in the garden,' he said. → He said (that) she was playing in the garden. (Present Continuous → Past Continuous)
'They have bought a new house,' he said. → He said (that) they had bought a new house. (Present Perfect → Past Perfect)
'He sent me flowers,' she said. → She said (that) he had sent her flowers. (Past Simple → Past Perfect)
'I'll order a new fridge,' he said. → He said (that) he would order a new fridge. (Future Simple → would)
today → that day; now → then; yesterday → the day before; tomorrow → the following day; ago → before; this → that

patterns.formula: KIM + said, 'I + HOZIRGI ZAMON.' → KIM + said (that) + he/she + O'TGAN ZAMON.
patterns.exampleEn: Ed said, 'I live in Belfast.' → Ed said that he lived in Belfast.
patterns.exampleUz: Ed 'Belfastda yashayman' dedi. → Ed Belfastda yashashini aytdi.

patterns.formula: 'I'll + FE'L,' he said. → He said (that) he would + FE'L.
patterns.exampleEn: 'I'll order a new fridge,' he said. → He said he would order a new fridge.
patterns.exampleUz: 'Yangi muzlatgich buyurtma qilaman,' dedi u. → U yangi muzlatgich buyurtma qilishini aytdi.

patterns.exampleEn: She says that she loves animals.
